claim_boundary: Cycle-accurate RTL simulation (Verilator 5.050, --timing) of the die-side collective engines, DMA, behavioural VM and a synthesizable link layer (framing, CRC-32, credit return, Gray-code CDC FIFOs, deterministic release) on per-die clocks; the analog PHY, channel and the PHY's PCS/FEC pipelines are timing models whose constants are cited or ASSUMED in `links`.  Layer-0 collective descriptors are the emitted program; operands are the synthetic arithmetic stress fixture, not a model token.

hbm_p48_ss_prod.slot_basis: Product bytes one bench record slot stands for.  The bench moves one 64 B record a switch cycle on each ... one record = 749.7 B at the 0.9 TB/s port and this clock; gathers rounded up to whole records

hbm_p6_prod.slot_basis: Product bytes one bench record slot stands for.  The bench moves one 64 B record a switch cycle on each ... one record = 870.5 B at the 0.9 TB/s port and this clock; gathers rounded up to whole records

codeword_bits.source: RS(272,257) over GF(2^10): 272 x 10 bits; payload 257 x 10 = 2,570 bits (Ethernet Technology Consortium LL-FEC Specification 1.0, 2018)

flight_ns.source: 0.3 m of board trace at ~6.7 ns/m (technology.json rom_board_serdes channel decomposition; TI SCAA082A stripline 7.15 ps/mm)

lanes.source: rtl/rom/ot_rom_oneshot_px.sv header ('T1 links (13 lanes per die pair)'); configs/hardware/technology.json links.rom_board_serdes

pcs_clock_ns.source: PCS datapath at twice the codeword rate: a frame (codeword payload) is 2 cycles x 2 slots = 4 records of 547 bits + header + CRC-32 = 2,300 of 2,570 payload bits

rs272_decode_ns.source: RS(272,257) '~99ns' total at 50 Gb/s lanes (P. Sun, IEEE 802.3 50GE ad hoc, 2016) of which the 51 ns codeword store is lane-rate bound; the ~48 ns processing is kept, the store is the 1.87 ns 13-lane codeword time here (tools/sync_cost_table.py r-sun3cd, r-gustlin3ck)

rx_afe_dsp_ns.source: ADC-DSP receiver (CDR, FFE/DFE): technology.json rom_board_serdes names ~40-60 ns; mid value

rx_deskew_align_ns.source: PCS lane alignment and deskew FIFO

static_latency_variation_ns.source: PMA/PCS gearbox and deskew-FIFO pointer placement differ per link training (IEEE P802.3cd brown_3cd_03_1116 'skew variation'); ~3 PCS cycles

tx_pcs_fec_encode_ns.source: PCS + RS encoder + gearbox; 4 PCS-clock register stages

board_112g.what: 112G PAM4 board SerDes between the two packages of a TP-4 group, 13 lanes per die pair, light RS(272,257) FEC

wire_stages_v41.source: results/floorplan/v41_pack_expanded_woa.json latency_crossings 'COLLECTIVE -> farthest SerDes lane' 24,911 um at 0.76 ps/um and 0.92 ns: tools/uarch_model.wire_cycles(24911.3, 1/0.92e-9, 0.76) = 29

fdi_clock_ns.source: D2D adapter / FDI clock of 1 GHz: the link-layer logic runs on it (a 2-slot frame per cycle, 2 x 547-bit records + header; 3.4 Tb/s of the 34.8 Tb/s raw)

modules.source: results/floorplan/v41_rtl_engine_profile.json gaps: 'UCIe-A modules (17)'; configs/hardware/technology.json links.rom_package_ucie.bytes_s 4.2 TB/s / (64 lanes x 32 GT/s / 8 = 256 GB/s per module)

phy_adapter_measured_ns.source: 3.5 ns FDI-to-FDI measured, 3 nm CoWoS UCIe-A, IEEE JSSC 2026, doi:10.1109/JSSC.2026.3651425 (sensitivity)

phy_adapter_tx_rx_ns.source: UCIe key metric 'Latency (Tx + Rx) < 2ns Includes D2D Adapter and PHY (FDI to bump and back)': D. Das Sharma et al., IEEE Trans. CPMT 12(9), 2022, Table I (tools/sync_cost_table.py r-ucie-tcpmt)

static_latency_variation_ns.source: half an FDI cycle of training-dependent PHY/adapter latency

ucie_a.what: UCIe-A (advanced package) die-to-die link inside a package, 17 x64 modules at 32 GT/s

wire_stages_qwen.source: tools/uarch_model.QWEN_WIRE ucie_wire_per_token (13 stages each way, W5) scaled by the loaded-channel ratio wscale = 1.29 (qwen_eval)

wire_stages_v41.source: results/floorplan/v41_pack_expanded_woa.json latency_crossings 'COLLECTIVE -> farthest UCIe module' 19,183 um, re-derived at 0.76 ps/um (tools/uarch_model.WIRE_PS_PER_UM_LOADED) and 0.92 ns: tools/uarch_model.wire_cycles(19183.4, 1/0.92e-9, 0.76) = 22

reading_guide.determinism: deterministic.distinct_timings == 1 over all det runs (seeds and the channel-corner runs), all results checked against the golden on every die
reading_guide.fit: configs.<cfg>.fit.{all_gather,all_reduce}.{fixed_cycles,cycles_per_word}: least squares over the ops; a word is one bench record (64 B, 16 FP32 lanes) per rank
reading_guide.per_op: configs.<cfg>.collectives[]: issue_to_last_commit_cycles = earliest issue on any die -> last result committed on the slowest die (all 2P dies), at clock_hz
reading_guide.product_bytes: the bench moves one record a switch cycle on each package downlink, and its frame carries a whole record, so timing does not depend on record width; the _prod configs time a product gather of B bytes a rank as ceil(B / slot_bytes) records, slot_bytes = 0.9 TB/s port x clock period (750.4 B at 1.2 GHz, 870.5 B at 1.034 GHz). Use cycles = fixed_cycles + cycles_per_word x ceil(B_per_rank / slot_bytes) for a product gather; the 64 B-word slope (~90 cycles a word a rank at P=48) is the BENCH width, not the product port
reading_guide.provenance: campaigns[configs[cfg].provenance] gives the git head and source pins of the run
